findings.title: Slots inside a date override skip busy checks and can double-book
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable now returns true as soon as a slot falls on a day with a date override and is treated as inside that override, before the busy-interval scan. That scan is the only place calendar conflicts and existing Cal bookings are applied to generated slots, and this function now runs for every fixed host — including ordinary personal and collective events, whose users are marked isFixed. On any day that has a date override, a slot inside the override is therefore shown as free even when the host is already booked, so the same time can be booked twice.

findings.title: Working-hours gate frees non-working days and drops split shifts
findings.body: The new working-hours check uses find() to look for a same-day window that does not contain the slot, and treats "no such window" as available. If a fixed host has no entry for that weekday, every callback is falsy, find returns undefined, and the slot is kept. That is the round-robin case this PR is meant to close: union slots from a rotating host stay bookable on days the fixed host does not work. The same predicate rejects valid slots when a host has two windows on one day (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00): the window that does not contain the slot makes find succeed and the slot is removed, so lunch-break schedules disappear from the booking page for every fixed host, not only round-robin. end is also copied from slotStartTime (line 142) instead of slotEndTime, so a slot that starts inside the window but runs past endTime is still treated as inside. A single window that fully contains the slot start still passes, which is why the existing one-range tests do not catch this.

findings.title: Override window test misses blocked days, partial overlaps, and extra ranges
findings.body: A full-day block is stored as an override whose start equals its end, and this callback tries to reject the whole day in that case. The comparison uses === on two dayjs objects, which is reference equality and is never true, so that branch never runs. The following checks only mark a slot outside a window when the slot ends at or before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that merely overlaps the window — starts before it, ends after it, or straddles a zero-length block — is treated as inside. find() then stops at the first same-day range that does not contain the slot, so two override ranges on one day (a normal custom-hours override with a gap) reject a slot that sits inside the other range and the day shows no bookable override slots. The date match also uses only the adjusted start, so an override whose UTC interval crosses midnight does not cover slots on the second day. After a timezone shift, a midnight–midnight block can land on the previous UTC date and miss the intended day entirely, leaving a fixed host bookable on a day they marked unavailable.

findings.title: Override date match compares server-local date to UTC date
findings.body: Whether an override applies to a slot is decided by formatting the offset-adjusted start with a local-mode dayjs and comparing it to slotStartTime.format(), and slotStartTime is in UTC mode (time.utc()). format() on a local-mode instance uses the process timezone, not UTC. Whenever the server timezone is not UTC, the two calendar dates disagree for overrides near midnight and the override is applied to the wrong day or not applied at all, so fixed-host date overrides silently fail outside a UTC process.

findings.title: Timezone-adjusted overrides drop the day and can wipe that day's hours
findings.body: Override start/end are converted by adding the invitee-minus-organizer offset and then keeping only hour and minute. That throws away a day boundary. If the shift moves one end across midnight and not the other, endTime is less than startTime; buildSlots discards any range with start >= end. The caller has already deleted that user's normal working hours for the invitee day the raw UTC timestamp fell on, so the day is left with no slots. Even when both ends wrap to clock times on the same side of midnight, the activeOverrides filter (line 206) still selects the invitee day that contains the unadjusted timestamp, whose UTC clock is the organizer wall time rather than the real instant. For a non-zero organizer offset those are different instants, so an evening override viewed from a timezone ahead (US host, European booker) is attached to the wrong calendar day. The new +6 test only shifts IST 14:00–18:00 by 30 minutes and stays on the same day, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Already-adjusted override minutes are DST-shifted again in buildSlots
findings.body: The new override minutes are computed from the override date's own organizer and invitee offsets, so they are already invitee-local minutes for that date. They are then pushed into computedLocalAvailability and passed through buildSlots, which adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff. That correction exists for working hours converted with today's offset (dayjs.tz(dayjs(), timeZone)), not for values already adjusted to the target date. When today and the booking day sit on different sides of a DST transition and the invitee timezone does not have the same delta, override slots move by an hour. Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Dhaka do not observe DST, so the added test cannot see it.

findings.title: Tests never exercise fixed-host overrides or a real timezone day shift
findings.body: The only new assertion re-requests the existing personal-event IST override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants. That is a 30-minute shift that stays inside one calendar day and never hits checkIfIsAvailable's fixed-host path with a host who is actually isFixed. Nothing covers a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override or weekday hours are narrower than the rotating host, a blocked day (start equal to end), a booking or calendar conflict on an override day, split windows, or an override that crosses midnight after timezone conversion. The scenario helper also never attaches eventType.hosts as {isFixed, user}, so the existing round-robin tests leave every user isFixed false and would not exercise this gate even if a case were added. The regressions above can merge green.
